study type: secondary analysis of a cross-sectional study
cohort: The study included data from 314,623 women who delivered in 359 health facilities across 29 countries in Africa, Asia, Latin America, and the Middle East.
finding: This analysis supports the concept of obstetric transition, showing that medicalization (including cesarean deliveries and labor inductions) and the mean age of primiparous women increased with higher obstetric transition stages, while female fertility and uterine rupture decreased.
mod_finding: Cesarean deliveries increased by 2.4 times (from 15.3% to 36.7%) and labor inductions increased by 2.6 times (from 7.1% to 18.8%) as countries transitioned from Obstetric Transition Stage II to Stage IV.
country: 29 countries in Africa, Asia, Latin America, and the Middle East
